newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire students bury dead from protest clash.
newsitem.headline: Zaire students bury dead from protest clash.

text.p: Armed Zairean troops encircled a university campus on Friday and blocked off roads to control angry students burying two comrades killed in anti-government protests, witnesses said.
"There were soldiers lined up all the way along one of the main boulevards in town," said freelance photographer Carlos Palma. "It was impossible for the students to go anywhere but the cemetery."

Earlier students said they would stop a planned cabinet meeting by matching to the office of Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo, a half-Tutsi accused of being soft on an ethnic Tutsi rebellion in eastern Zaire.
The presence of heavily armed troops prevented students from carrying out their threat.
Demonstrators have attacked Tutsi homes and property in the past week and vowed war against neighbouring Rwanda, whose Tutsi-led army is accused by Zaire of helping the rebels.
Rebels have seized control of two Zairean provinces bordering Rwanda and Burundi in three weeks of fighting.
On Thursday thousands of students bearing the coffins of the two dead colleagues took over the parliament building, calling for Kengo's resignation.

The students are allied to radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi and want his reappointment as prime minister. Tshisekedi held the post briefly before he was sacked by President Mobutu Sese Seko in 1993.
Around 3,000 students wearing bandanas and carrying leaves and flowers attended Friday's funeral in the Gombe cemetery just outside central Kinshasa.
